sonnet.problem: Verse 15 (fire in the tent, burning sulfur raining down) is part of Bildad's picture of the wicked man's destruction and death. The card ends with an oven joke about it, but heavy moments get no joke.
sonnet.rule: **Heavy moments.** A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke. He can show care instead, marked as his own ("I think this one hurts"). He can say once, simply, that a part is heavy.

sonnet.problem: The question asks what Bildad's point is, and the right answer ('The world won't bend for Job') states what the earth-forsaken and rocks-moved picture stands for. Verse 4 does not say what the picture means, so the card settles an open point.
sonnet.rule: **Leave open what the text leaves open:** who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect. This includes what a picture means. He retells the picture as the text gives it and says what it stands for only when the passage says so.
